notes: REVISION: originally published April 7, 2026, and updated July 22, 2026; revised paragraphs are tagged '(New, July 22, 2026)' or '(Updated, July 22, 2026)'. The update added detection guidance for malicious changes to AOIs (the 'reusable code modules leveraged within Rockwell Automation PLC programs', analogous to 'Function Block'/'User Defined Function Block'). It also expanded the targeted manufacturers to Schneider Electric and Siemens. A good output records both dates. ATTRIBUTION: the current activity is attributed only to 'Iranian-affiliated APT actors', with 'assess' wording. CyberAv3ngers, its aliases (Shahid Kaveh Group, Hydro Kitten, Storm-0784, APT Iran, Bauxite, Mr. Soul, Soldiers of Solomon, UNC5691) and the IRGC Cyber Electronic Command appear only in connection with previously reported 'similar activity'. That earlier campaign began in November 2023, targeted U.S.-based Unitronics PLCs and compromised 'at least 75 devices'. A model stating that CyberAv3ngers or IRGC-CEC conducts the current campaign overstates the text; noting the link or similarity is correct. Coding A3 because IRGC CEC is named is wrong. CyberAv3ngers is coded kind=affiliate_label because the text calls it 'a cyber threat actor affiliated with' IRGC CEC and never uses 'persona'; persona or alias are tolerable codings for scoring. The aliases are aliases of CyberAv3ngers, not of the primary 'Iranian-affiliated APT actors'. REGIONS: Israel appears only in the motive clause ('hostilities between Iran, and the United States and Israel'), not as a target. Iran is the actor side. 'foreign-based IP addresses' and 'leased, third-party hosted infrastructure' are actor infrastructure. TOOLS/CVEs: no CVEs and no malware family names appear. The abused tools are legitimate vendor engineering/configuration software, plus Dropbear SSH on victim modems (one reported instance, so non-core). Unnamed malicious artifacts: a malicious project file, logic overriding safety-related instruction sets, disabled critical shutdown and alarm logic, and custom ladder logic code (2023 campaign). Ports 44818, 2222, 102 and 502 (PLCs) and 22 (modems) are technical details, not schema items. Unitronics PLCs belong to the 2023 campaign (historical, non-core). TEXT ARTIFACTS: the line 'For a downloadable copy of historical April 7, 2026 IOCs, see:' has no link text after it in the input. The '1' after 'PLC project files' is a footnote marker. IMPACT (not a schema item): operational disruption and financial loss at some victims; data manipulation on HMI/SCADA displays. Referenced prior advisory, a document title and not an item: 'IRGC-Affiliated Cyber Actors Exploit PLCs in Multiple Sectors, Including US Water and Wastewater Systems Facilities'. Category alternates: Dropbear SSH is coded rmm_or_legit_software, but commodity_or_open_source_tool is acceptable. The three vendor engineering suites are legitimate software abused, not malware.
